2607.25497.title: Beyond Counts: A Distributional Robustness Margin For Pathology Foundation Models
2607.25497.paper_summary: Pathology foundation models are approaching clinical deployment, yet remain vulnerable to systematic non-biological variation across centres. Differences in tissue preparation, staining and scanning are strongly encoded in their representations, enabling shortcut learning and weakening generalisation across cohorts and institutions. The Robustness Index (RI) quantifies whether local representation geometry is dominated by biology or by non-biological variation, but its count-based formulation discards distance information. We show that adding distance weights changes little because the deeper limitation lies in RI's pooled, fixed-neighbourhood design, which obscures sample-level heterogeneity and effectively evaluates only a model-dependent subset of samples. We introduce the Cross-confounder Robustness Margin (CRoMa), a sample-resolved measure that directly compares distances to cross-confounder biological matches and same-confounder biological distractors. CRoMa recasts robustness as a cohort-wide margin distribution rather than a single pooled score. We evaluated frozen representations from 20 tile-level encoders across three benchmarks and 4 slide-level encoders on a fourth. Rankings by median CRoMa were broadly consistent across datasets, while the underlying distributions revealed substantial within-model heterogeneity. Every tile encoder retained a confounder-dominated lower tail, whose prevalence and severity varied markedly across models. These distinct robustness profiles frame model selection as a Pareto trade-off between typical and lower-tail robustness. Higher CRoMa was also associated with smaller shortcut-induced performance drops after supervised adaptation. By turning representation geometry into a distributional robustness readout that anticipates downstream shortcut susceptibility, CRoMa provides a principled basis for robustness assessment and model selection.
2607.25497.paper_summary_zh: 病理基礎模型正在接近臨床部署，但仍然容易受到各中心之間系統性非生物變異的影響。組織準備、染色和掃描的差異在其表徵中強烈編碼，這使得捷徑學習成為可能，並削弱了跨隊列和機構的泛化能力。穩健性指數（RI）量化了局部表徵幾何是否受到生物學或非生物變異的主導，但其基於計數的公式捨棄了距離信息。我們顯示，添加距離權重的變化不大，因為更深層的限制在於RI的合併固定鄰域設計，這掩蓋了樣本級異質性，並有效地僅評估模型依賴的樣本子集。我們引入了交叉混淆穩健性邊際（CRoMa），這是一種樣本解析的度量，直接比較與交叉混淆生物匹配和同混淆生物干擾者的距離。CRoMa將穩健性重新表述為整體隊列的邊際分佈，而不是單一的合併分數。我們評估了來自20個瓷磚級編碼器的凍結表徵，涵蓋三個基準，並在第四個基準上評估了4個幻燈片級編碼器。按中位數CRoMa進行的排名在數據集之間大致一致，而潛在的分佈顯示出模型內部的顯著異質性。每個瓷磚編碼器都保留了一個以混淆因子主導的下尾，其普遍性和嚴重性在模型之間顯著不同。這些不同的穩健性輪廓將模型選擇框架化為典型和下尾穩健性之間的帕累托權衡。更高的CRoMa也與經過監督適應後較小的捷徑引起的性能下降相關。通過將表徵幾何轉化為預測下游捷徑易感性的分佈穩健性讀數，CRoMa為穩健性評估和模型選擇提供了原則性的基礎。
